headline: Medium risk: Airbyte can exfiltrate business data while PaddleOCR processes documents/images, creating default-path leakage and downstream trust risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, Airbyte can move business data through APIs and PaddleOCR can run browsers and process documents/images, so a manual copy-paste or file handoff could carry malicious instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies Airbyte-exported text into PaddleOCR inputs, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace or clipboard is introduced, attacker-controlled content can bridge the agents.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable browser use for PaddleOCR unless needed.
Strip instructions from any text passed between agents.
Use a human review step before forwarding outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and touches business data; PaddleOCR processes documents and images and also has network egress, so sensitive content can flow through both systems in default workflows. No shared filesystem is documented, but the pair can still leak data through uploaded documents, API calls, or OCR outputs. Uncertainty about exact deployment should not lower severity.
conditions: IF business data is routed from Airbyte into PaddleOCR, the OCR output may expose document contents.
IF either agent sends processed content to a third-party API, leakage can occur.
mitigations: Minimize sensitive fields before transfer.
Route both agents through a private network only.
Disable external uploads where possible.
Review logs for document text and redact them.
Use synthetic samples for testing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have network egress, but the profiles do not show shared writable storage, git state, or overlapping mutable OAuth scopes. Airbyte is API-oriented and PaddleOCR is document-processing oriented, so direct write-write conflict is not established. The main overlap is network use, which is not enough for a higher severity here.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API resource, conflicts can occur.
IF a shared output directory is added, concurrent writes may collide.
mitigations: Assign separate output destinations.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Add file or record locking if a shared sink is used.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same dataset.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data that PaddleOCR may consume as document input or derived text, and PaddleOCR can then emit OCR results that downstream systems may trust. No verification or provenance controls are documented, so errors can cascade across the pair. Because the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR consumes Airbyte output without validation, upstream errors can propagate.
IF downstream automation treats OCR text as authoritative, incorrect records can be acted on.
mitigations: Insert schema validation between agents.
Require human review for high-impact outputs.
Compare OCR results against source documents.
Log provenance for each transferred record.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and PaddleOCR touches documents/images, but the profiles do not show residency, certification, or retention mismatches. With only docs-level evidence, a compliance issue is possible if regulated documents are routed through the pair, yet no specific breach is established. The other agent is cited because the risk depends on both data paths.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are routed through both agents, policy mismatches may arise.
IF one agent retains outputs longer than the other, retention obligations can diverge.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it.
Set a shared retention policy.
Block regulated data from test runs.
Document residency and retention for both systems.
